title: Warranty - Phones, International Service
text:
This warranty explains international service for phones bought from our store, whether you ordered online or bought in person. When service is requested outside the United States, phones are not covered: the maker does not offer warranty service for these phones abroad, so no repair, replacement or refund is given under this warranty for a fault reported while the phone is outside the United States. This holds whatever the fault is and however long ago the phone was bought.

What international service covers

International service covers no faults. A screen that stops responding to touch, buttons or ports that stop working, a battery that will no longer hold a charge, and a phone that will not turn on are all outside this warranty when the service is requested abroad, even when the fault comes from materials or workmanship rather than from an accident. The charger and cable that came in the box are treated in the same way as the phone itself, and so are faults that appear in the first days after purchase. If a fault starts while you are travelling, stop using a phone that overheats or swells, and stop using a charger that sparks or smells of burning.

What is not covered

Because international service is not covered, this warranty pays for no parts, labor, shipping or customs charges for a repair arranged outside the United States. Fees that a local shop or network charges just to check the phone are not covered either. Cracked screens, liquid damage, damage from drops or other accidents, normal wear, faults caused by software or apps you installed, and lost or stolen phones are not covered in any case. Accessories bought separately, such as cases and screen protectors, carry their own terms, and a phone whose identification number has been removed or changed is never covered.

Asking for help abroad

You cannot make a warranty claim for international service. You can still contact our customer service team online for advice while you are abroad: describe the fault and, if you can, send a short video or photo that shows it. A team member may suggest a restart, a software update or a change of settings, because many faults clear without any repair at all. The team answers by email or chat, usually within a few business days. Keep a note of the case number we give you, and quote it whenever you contact us about the same fault.

Repairs arranged abroad

If you decide to have the phone repaired by a local shop outside the United States, you choose the shop and you pay for the repair yourself, and the cost is never refunded under this warranty. A local repair may use parts that are not the maker's own, so ask the shop which parts it uses before it starts work, and keep its invoice. A repair by anyone other than an approved service center is not covered either. Back up the phone and remove your SIM card before you hand it over, and check that no account or payment card is still linked to it.

Proof of purchase and transfer

Keep your proof of purchase, because it shows where and when the phone was bought, and it is the first thing our team asks for when you contact us for advice from abroad. The terms on this page stay with the phone if you give it away or sell it, and they apply to the next owner in the same way. If you bought online with your account, our team can find the sale there if the proof is lost.
